questions.question: The resting membrane potential of a nerve fibre is mainly due to:

options.B: Potassium efflux through leak channels and the Na⁺–K⁺ pump

questions.explanation: The membrane is far more permeable to K⁺ at rest; the Na⁺/K⁺ ATPase pumps 3 Na⁺ out and 2 K⁺ in.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The upstroke (depolarisation) of the action potential in a nerve is due to:

options.A: Rapid sodium influx through voltage-gated channels

questions.explanation: Repolarisation is due to inactivation of Na⁺ channels and K⁺ efflux.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: During the absolute refractory period of a nerve:

options.B: No stimulus, however strong, can produce another action potential
options.D: A stronger-than-normal stimulus can produce a response

questions.explanation: It limits the maximum frequency of firing and ensures one-way conduction.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Saltatory conduction occurs in:

options.C: Myelinated nerve fibres, with the impulse jumping between nodes of Ranvier

questions.explanation: It is faster and more energy efficient than continuous conduction.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which nerve fibre type has the fastest conduction velocity?
questions.explanation: A-alpha (proprioception and motor, 70–120 m/s); A-delta carries fast pain; C fibres carry slow pain.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Wallerian degeneration occurs in the:

options.A: Distal segment of a nerve fibre after transection

questions.explanation: The axon and myelin degenerate distal to the injury; regeneration proceeds at about 1–1.5 mm per day.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Curare paralyses skeletal muscle by:

options.A: Blocking calcium channels in the nerve terminal
options.C: Competitively blocking nicotinic acetylcholine receptors at the motor end plate

questions.explanation: Succinylcholine is a depolarising blocker; neostigmine reverses non-depolarising blocks.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: During muscle contraction, the sarcomere shortens because:

options.D: Actin filaments slide over myosin filaments, shortening the I-band and H-zone

questions.explanation: The A-band length stays constant.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In skeletal muscle, calcium triggers contraction by binding to:
questions.explanation: Calcium binding to troponin C shifts tropomyosin, exposing myosin-binding sites on actin.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Rigor mortis occurs because of:

options.A: Lack of ATP, preventing detachment of myosin heads from actin

questions.explanation: ATP is needed for cross-bridge detachment.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Type I (slow oxidative) muscle fibres are characterised by:

options.C: High myoglobin, many mitochondria and resistance to fatigue

questions.explanation: Postural muscles such as soleus are rich in type I fibres.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A motor unit consists of:

options.A: A sensory neurone and a muscle
options.B: A motor neurone and all the muscle fibres it innervates

questions.explanation: Muscles of fine control (e.g. eye muscles) have small motor units.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Tetanus in skeletal muscle is produced by:

options.C: High-frequency stimulation causing fusion of individual twitches

questions.explanation: Temporal summation; cardiac muscle cannot be tetanised because of its long refractory period.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The immediate source of energy for muscle contraction during the first few seconds of intense activity is:
questions.explanation: ATP stores last about 3 seconds; phosphocreatine lasts about 10 seconds; then glycolysis.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In an isometric contraction of a muscle:

options.D: Tension increases but muscle length remains constant

questions.explanation: No external work is done.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The normal haemoglobin concentration in an adult male is about:
questions.explanation: Adult female: 12–15 g/dL; anaemia is defined as <13 in men and <12 in women.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The average lifespan of a red blood cell is:
questions.explanation: Old RBCs are removed by the spleen.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Erythropoietin is mainly produced by the:
questions.explanation: Hypoxia stimulates its release; the stimulus for RBC production.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Haemolytic disease of the newborn occurs when:

options.A: An Rh-negative mother carries an Rh-positive fetus (second pregnancy onwards)
options.D: An Rh-positive mother carries an Rh-negative fetus

questions.explanation: Anti-D immunoglobulin is given to prevent sensitisation.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The normal platelet count is:
questions.explanation: Spontaneous bleeding can occur when below 20,000/µL.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which clotting factor is deficient in haemophilia B (Christmas disease)?
questions.explanation: Factor VIII: haemophilia A; factor IX: haemophilia B.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Vitamin K is necessary for synthesis of clotting factors:
questions.explanation: Warfarin acts by antagonising vitamin K.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The commonest white blood cell in adult peripheral blood is the:
questions.explanation: Neutrophils (40–75%), lymphocytes (20–45%), monocytes (2–10%), eosinophils (1–6%), basophils (<1%).
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Cardiac output is the product of:
questions.explanation: Normal about 5 L/min at rest (70 mL × 72 bpm).
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The Frank–Starling law of the heart states that:

options.C: Contractility depends on the nerve supply only
options.D: Within limits, the force of contraction increases with increased end-diastolic fibre length

questions.explanation: Greater venous return increases stroke volume.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The natural pacemaker of the heart is the:
questions.explanation: SA node discharges at 70–80/min; AV node about 40–60/min.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In a normal ECG the QRS complex represents:
questions.explanation: P wave: atrial depolarisation; T wave: ventricular repolarisation.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The second heart sound (S2) is caused by:

options.A: Closure of the mitral and tricuspid valves
options.D: Closure of the aortic and pulmonary valves

questions.explanation: S1 marks the start of systole; S3 is rapid ventricular filling (normal in children).
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Mean arterial pressure is approximately:

options.C: Diastolic pressure plus one-third of the pulse pressure

questions.explanation: MAP = DBP + (SBP−DBP)/3; e.g. 120/80 → 93 mmHg.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A sudden rise in arterial blood pressure causes baroreceptor stimulation leading to:
questions.explanation: Located in the carotid sinus and aortic arch; the glossopharyngeal and vagus nerves carry the afferents.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: During dynamic exercise, which cardiovascular change occurs?

options.D: Increase in heart rate, stroke volume and systolic blood pressure

questions.explanation: Diastolic pressure remains unchanged or falls slightly due to vasodilatation in muscles.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Maximum coronary blood flow to the left ventricle occurs during:
questions.explanation: During systole intramyocardial pressure compresses the coronary vessels.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The volume of air inspired or expired during a normal quiet breath is the:
questions.explanation: Vital capacity = IRV + TV + ERV (~4.5–5 L).
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The volume of air remaining in the lungs after a maximal expiration is the:
questions.explanation: It cannot be measured by simple spirometry; helium dilution or body plethysmography is used.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Functional residual capacity is the sum of:

options.A: Inspiratory reserve volume and tidal volume
options.C: Expiratory reserve volume and residual volume

questions.explanation: FRC is the volume remaining in the lungs after a normal quiet expiration.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Surfactant, produced by type II pneumocytes, acts by:

options.B: Reducing alveolar surface tension and preventing collapse

questions.explanation: Deficiency causes neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (hyaline membrane disease).
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A rightward shift of the oxygen dissociation curve is caused by:

options.C: Increased CO₂, increased temperature, decreased pH and increased 2,3-DPG

questions.explanation: A right shift (Bohr effect) reduces haemoglobin affinity for oxygen and releases more O₂ to tissues.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The primary respiratory rhythm generator is located in the:
questions.explanation: The pneumotaxic centre in the pons modulates the inspiratory time.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The most potent stimulus for the central chemoreceptors is an increase in:

options.B: Hydrogen ion concentration in the CSF due to raised PaCO₂

questions.explanation: Peripheral chemoreceptors (carotid and aortic bodies) respond mainly to low PaO₂.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Anatomical dead space in a healthy adult is approximately:
questions.explanation: Alveolar ventilation = (TV − dead space) × RR.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: At the onset of heavy exercise, the increase in ventilation is initially due to:

options.C: Cortical and proprioceptive stimuli from moving limbs

questions.explanation: Chemical changes are not great enough in moderate exercise.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The normal glomerular filtration rate in a healthy adult is about:
questions.explanation: About 180 L/day; 99% is reabsorbed.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) acts on the:
questions.explanation: Deficiency causes diabetes insipidus with polyuria and low urine osmolality.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Renin is secreted by the:

options.C: Juxtaglomerular cells of the afferent arteriole

questions.explanation: Renin converts angiotensinogen to angiotensin I; ACE converts it to angiotensin II.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Most of the filtered glucose is reabsorbed in the:
questions.explanation: SGLT2 reabsorbs glucose; glycosuria occurs when the renal threshold (~180 mg/dL) is exceeded.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Hydrochloric acid in the stomach is secreted by the:
questions.explanation: Chief cells secrete pepsinogen; G cells secrete gastrin.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Intrinsic factor is necessary for absorption of:

options.D: Vitamin B12 in the terminal ileum

questions.explanation: Deficiency leads to pernicious anaemia.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Bile salts are essential for:
questions.explanation: Cholecystokinin causes gallbladder contraction.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Most nutrient absorption in the gastrointestinal tract occurs in the:
questions.explanation: The surface area is greatly increased by villi and microvilli.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Insulin is secreted by the:

options.A: Beta cells of the islets of Langerhans

questions.explanation: Glucagon is secreted by alpha cells; somatostatin by delta cells.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The most active form of thyroid hormone is:
questions.explanation: T4 is secreted in larger amounts and converted peripherally to T3.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Parathyroid hormone (PTH) acts to:

options.C: Raise plasma calcium by increasing bone resorption and renal reabsorption and activating vitamin D

questions.explanation: Calcitonin lowers plasma calcium.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Cortisol secretion shows a diurnal rhythm with the peak at:
questions.explanation: It increases blood glucose, suppresses inflammation and mobilises protein.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Excess growth hormone in adults causes:
questions.explanation: In children before epiphyseal closure it causes gigantism.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The stretch reflex (knee jerk) is a:
questions.explanation: Muscle spindle Ia afferent synapses directly on the alpha motor neurone.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The flexor withdrawal reflex is mediated by:

options.A: Polysynaptic pathways with reciprocal inhibition and crossed extensor reflex

questions.explanation: Painful stimulus: flexion of the stimulated limb, extension of the opposite limb.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which finding is characteristic of an upper motor neurone lesion?

options.B: Spasticity, hyperreflexia and an extensor plantar response

questions.explanation: LMN lesions: flaccid paralysis, wasting, fasciculations, absent reflexes.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The gate control theory of pain was proposed by:
questions.explanation: Large diameter A-beta input closes the gate in the substantia gelatinosa to inhibit pain transmission — basis of TENS.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Pain from myocardial ischaemia referred to the left arm is explained by:

options.D: Convergence of visceral and somatic afferents on the same spinal segments

questions.explanation: Convergence-projection theory; phrenic irritation is referred to the shoulder tip (C3–C5).
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Dreaming occurs mainly in:
questions.explanation: Paradoxical sleep with rapid eye movements and loss of muscle tone.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The body's thermoregulatory centre is located in the:
questions.explanation: The anterior hypothalamus mediates heat loss; the posterior hypothalamus mediates heat conservation.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Night vision (scotopic vision) is mediated by:
questions.explanation: Cones mediate colour vision and visual acuity in daylight; rhodopsin needs vitamin A.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The audible frequency range of the normal human ear is about:
questions.explanation: Ultrasound is above 20 kHz.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Maximal oxygen uptake (VO₂ max) is best described as:

options.A: The amount of oxygen in arterial blood
options.B: The highest rate at which the body can consume oxygen during maximal dynamic exercise

questions.explanation: It is the best measure of aerobic fitness; limited by cardiac output.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The anaerobic (lactate) threshold is the exercise intensity at which:

options.D: Blood lactate begins to accumulate rapidly

questions.explanation: Training raises the threshold and improves endurance.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
